title: Black Pepper Custard Ice Cream
changes_from_base: Coarse black pepper steeped in the dairy instead of vanilla, and the custard cooked to 77-80 °C rather than only tempered.
summary: Our classic custard with coarse black pepper steeped in the dairy instead of vanilla. Creamy and sweet up front with a warm, tingly finish; great with strawberries or chocolate desserts.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Infuse the pepper
steps.text: Bring the cream, milk, sugar and pepper to the boil, then cover and leave off the heat for 15 min.

steps.title: Whisk the yolks
steps.text: Whisk the yolks and salt until light.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Reheat the pepper dairy until steaming and pour it gradually into the yolks, whisking all the time, then return everything to the pan.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Stir over low heat until the speckled custard thickens and reaches 77-80 °C.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Strain for a smooth ice cream, or skip the sieve for black speckles. Cool in the iced water and chill for at least 4 h.

steps.title: Churn and freeze
steps.text: Churn, then freeze for at least 4 h.

tips: Grind the pepper fresh and coarse; pre-ground pepper tastes dusty.
A common mistake is using too much pepper; the heat builds as it sits.
Try a scoop on fresh strawberries.
storage: Freeze, covered, for up to 2 weeks.
